uncited: Volumetric Code-Block EBCOT extends the Embedded Block Coding with Optimized Truncation (EBCOT) algorithm by allowing code-blocks to have a depth greater than one, enabling the exploitation of inter-slice correlations in volumetric data.
Unlike standard JPEG 2000 Part 1 or Part 2, which restrict code-blocks to a flat 2D geometry (depth=1), this method supports 3D code-blocks (depth>1) as implemented in the JP3D standard.

It sets itself apart by allowing the arithmetic coder to adapt to the statistical properties of 3D input volumes, offering significant compression gains over 2D block coding for medical volumetric data.
- Input: A set of 3D wavelet coefficients resulting from a 3D discrete wavelet transform (DWT) applied to volumetric data.
- **Code-Block:** A 3D array of wavelet coefficients.
The dimensions are defined as Width ($W$), Height ($H$), and Depth ($D$).

- **Bit-Plane Coding Contexts:** Standard EBCOT contexts are used, but the spatial neighborhood for context modeling includes coefficients from adjacent slices (depth dimension) in addition to the current slice.
- **Code-Block Size:** The dimensions $W \times H \times D$.
**Partitioning:** Partition the 3D wavelet subbands into 3D code-blocks of size $W \times H \times D$.
**Bit-Plane Generation:** For each code-block, generate bit-planes from the most significant bit (MSB) to the least significant bit (LSB).
**Context Modeling:** For each coefficient in the current bit-plane, determine its significance state based on the significance of its neighbors.
- Spatial neighbors in the same slice ($x \pm 1, y \pm 1$).
- Temporal/Depth neighbors in adjacent slices ($z \pm 1$) if the code-block depth $D > 1$ and the neighbor is within the same code-block.
**Arithmetic Coding:** Encode the significance and magnitude information using the arithmetic coder.
**Rate-Distortion Optimization (RDO):** Determine the truncation point for each code-block to maximize the rate-distortion performance.
**Bitstream Formatting:** Assemble the coded bits into the final bitstream, including headers for each code-block.
- **Code-Block Size > 32×32×32:** Using code-blocks larger than $32 \times 32 \times 32$ (e.g., $64 \times 64 \times 32$) causes a drop in coding performance.
- **Standard JPEG 2000 Compatibility:** Volumetric code-blocks are not supported by JPEG 2000 Part 1 or Part 2.
Assessment of code-block sizes for EBCOT to balance compression efficiency (long runs of bits for statistical model adaptation) and random access/RD-optimization granularity.
Code-block dimensions tested range from $16 \times 16 \times 1$ to $64 \times 64 \times 32$.
- **Time Complexity:** Not explicitly given, but depends on the number of coefficients and the arithmetic coding overhead.
Larger blocks reduce overhead per coefficient but increase memory usage for context modeling.
- **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the code-block size.
A $32 \times 32 \times 32$ block requires storing significance maps and contexts for 32,768 coefficients.

- **Measured Performance:** For medical volumetric data, switching from $16 \times 16 \times 1$ to $32 \times 32 \times 1$ improves compression efficiency by about 0.7 dB or 10% in bit-rate reduction.
Switching to $64 \times 64 \times 1$ improves it by about 1 dB.
Better adaptation of the arithmetic coder to 3D statistical properties.
Larger blocks reduce random access granularity.
- **When to use:** When compressing volumetric medical data and JP3D support is available.
- **When not to use:** When compatibility with standard JPEG 2000 is required or when random access granularity is critical and block sizes must be small.
Volumetric Code-Block EBCOT is a technique developed for the compression of volumetric medical images.
It is part of the JP3D standard, which extends JPEG 2000 to support 3D data.
The method leverages the 3D wavelet transform to exploit correlations between slices, and the EBCOT algorithm to provide embedded bitstreams with rate-distortion optimization.
